groups.title: Where places comes from (opens in new tab)
More about amendments to high needs places (opens in new tab)
The sub-total for each discretionary bursary element is calculated by multiplying the number of students by the instances per student to get the number of instances:
Total funded students × Instances per student = Number of instances
The number of instances is then multiplied by the rate:

The sub-totals are then added together to make your discretionary bursary fund total. This figure is then used in the next calculation. It is compared with your total discretionary bursary fund from @year-1 to @year0. It will be adjusted if it falls outside the limits set for this year.

@year-1 to @year0 Discretionary bursary fund (baseline for transition)
From @year0 to @year1, we moved to a new methodology to calculate your discretionary bursary fund.
In @year-1 to @year0, you received the amount shown in the first row of the adjusted discretionary bursary fund table. Going forward:
In @year0 to @year1, you received an amount capped between +/- 25% of the @year-1 to @year0 total
This year, you will receive an amount capped between +/- 50% of the @year-1 to @year0 total
In @year2 to 2023, you will receive an amount capped between +/- 75% of the @year-1 to @year0 total
2023 to 2024 onward - you receive the amount with no cap applied
